title: A held remote key repeats undo, clear and play/pause at key-repeat rate
body:
## Summary
MainActivity.onKeyDown ignored KeyEvent.repeatCount, so a held OK flipped play/pause per repeat and a held Up undid one stroke per repeat.

## Description
A held key arrives as a press plus a repeat every ~50 ms. The key map (tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/MainActivity.kt:135-155 before) turned every repeat into a fresh command. Undo walks the review's history (core TransportPlan.kt:71), so a one-second hold on Up undid about 13 strokes; a slightly long OK press toggled an odd or even number of times. Fixed: the map is remoteCommand(keyCode, repeatCount) (MainActivity.kt:170) and only seek+/seek- follow a hold; repeats of any other owned key are consumed and dropped. The stick-app round found the same defect in its own key bridge ("A held Select, Menu or Play repeats into the page as fresh presses").

## Flow
- viewer holds Up for a second -> 1 press + ~12 repeats -> onKeyDown -> 13 x Transport(undo) -> 13 strokes gone
- fix: remoteCommand ignores repeatCount > 0 except for the scrub keys; onKeyDown consumes the ignored repeats

## Expected impact
Anyone driving the Telestrator from the remote: a long press no longer erases a review or flips playback at random. Could break: a viewer who relied on hold-to-undo-many must now press repeatedly.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - one hold, one action, except scrubbing
Before: RemoteKeysTest on the old map: held Up (press + 12 repeats) -> 13 undos; held OK/Play-Pause -> 13 toggles; held Down -> 13 clears
After: same test on the fix: 1 undo, 1 toggle, 1 clear; held Right/Rewind still 13 seeks
Method: gate - RemoteKeysTest red on the old mapping ([undo x13]), green after; full tv-app gate exit 0 (24 tests)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/MainActivity.kt:170 remoteCommand(keyCode, repeatCount)
red: expected <[undo]> but was <[undo, undo, undo, undo, undo, undo, undo, undo, undo, undo, undo, undo, undo]>

title: A TV remote's separate Play and Pause keys were dead keys
body:
## Summary
Core plans "play" and "pause", but the remote key map only knew MEDIA_PLAY_PAUSE, so KEYCODE_MEDIA_PLAY and KEYCODE_MEDIA_PAUSE did nothing.

## Description
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/TransportPlan.kt:42-43 plans play and pause; the phone protocol can send them. The TV's key map (tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/MainActivity.kt) mapped only the combined key. A TV's own remote reaching the stick over HDMI-CEC has separate Play and Pause buttons, which arrive as KEYCODE_MEDIA_PLAY (126) and KEYCODE_MEDIA_PAUSE (127) and fell through to super.onKeyDown. Fixed: both are mapped to their verbs, and a held Pause pauses once.

## Flow
- viewer presses Pause on the TV's own remote -> KEYCODE_MEDIA_PAUSE -> no mapping -> nothing happens
- fix: remoteCommand maps MEDIA_PLAY -> play, MEDIA_PAUSE -> pause

## Expected impact
Viewers using the TV's remote over CEC can pause on the frame they want. Could break: nothing mapped them before.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the remote's Play and Pause keys play and pause
Before: MEDIA_PLAY -> null, MEDIA_PAUSE -> null; TransportPlan verbs reachable from the remote: 5 (toggle, seek+, seek-, undo, clear)
After: MEDIA_PLAY -> play, MEDIA_PAUSE -> pause; verbs reachable: 7 (commit body says 6 -> 8, which miscounted; 5 -> 7 is right)
Method: gate - RemoteKeysTest case red (expected <play> but was <null>), green after; tv-app gate exit 0 (25 tests). That CEC delivers these codes on a given TV is a device fact, unverified
Result: better
Gate: none

title: An unreachable relay showed the same invitation QR as a ready one
body:
## Summary
RelayTransport never set PenTransport.failure and its pairingUrl() is always non-null, so a relay the TV could not reach rendered as a valid invitation.

## Description
MainActivity's link poll (tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/MainActivity.kt:86-94) sends Failed when transport.failure is set, else Ready when pairingUrl() is non-null. LanTransport reports its bind failure that way; RelayTransport (tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/transport/RelayTransport.kt) only logged its failed dials and backed off, so 'cannot reach the relay' and 'ready' rendered identically: a QR to a meeting the TV would never attend. Technique: retry-backoff / retry-observability (failure is not an empty success). Fixed: three dials in a row that never reach the relay (~3.5 s at the existing backoff) set failure to 'The pen relay cannot be reached. Still trying.'; the next connected dial clears it and LinkState's Ready clears the card.

## Flow
- launch with --es transport relay while the relay is down -> dial fails, backoff, repeat -> pairingUrl() non-null -> card shows Invite forever
- fix: count consecutive dials that never connected; at 3 set failure; on connect clear it

## Expected impact
A viewer or the harness sees why pairing cannot work instead of scanning a dead QR. Could break: a relay that blinks for >3.5 s now covers the picture with the Failed card until it answers.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the card distinguishes 'relay unreachable' from 'ready'
Before: RelayFailureTest, nothing listening for 8 s: failure stays null (card: Invite)
After: failure set within 8 s; after a relay comes up on the port, failure null again within one backoff (test 7.4 s)
Method: gate - RelayFailureTest red ('an unreachable relay left failure null'), green after; tv-app gate exit 0 (27 tests). The Failed card on the TV is not captured
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/transport/RelayTransport.kt FAILED_DIALS = 3, UNREACHABLE
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/MainActivity.kt:88-91 (failure -> Failed, else url -> Ready)
coupled: tv-app/build.gradle.kts unitTests.isReturnDefaultValues = true

title: The pen socket read any frame size whole before a PIN was checked
body:
## Summary
The LAN pen server installed Ktor WebSockets with the default maxFrameSize (Long.MAX_VALUE), so any device on the Wi-Fi could send one frame of hundreds of megabytes into a Fire TV Stick's heap before pairing.

## Description
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/transport/LanTransport.kt installed WebSockets with no limit; KtorPenChannel.receiveLoop reads each text frame whole (PenTransport.kt) before PenSessionHost hands it to the pairing desk. A phone's messages are a few hundred bytes (a 16 ms batch of points, companion/index.html:447; a hello; a tag). The relay client had the same default for frames the relay forwards. Technique: device-pairing / admission-scoping (minimise the pre-trust surface). Fixed: MAX_PEN_FRAME_BYTES = 64 KiB caps both; the server module is Application.penServer(...) so a JVM test stands it up.

## Flow
- LAN neighbour opens ws://<tv>:8765/ws -> sends one 500 MB text frame -> Ktor buffers it -> readText -> the Stick runs out of heap before the hello is parsed
- fix: install(WebSockets) { maxFrameSize = 64 KiB } on the server and the relay client

## Expected impact
The TV app survives a hostile or broken client on the LAN or behind the relay. Could break: a legitimate message over 64 KiB (none exists today) would drop the pen's connection.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - an oversized frame is dropped unread
Before: PenFrameLimitTest (real CIO server and client on 127.0.0.1): a 1 MiB frame reaches the pen loop whole (received [1048576])
After: the 1 MiB frame is dropped unread (received [], connection closed); a 2 000-char frame still reads
Method: gate - PenFrameLimitTest red ('the server read a 1 MiB frame'), green after; tv-app gate exit 0 (29 tests). Not measured: the frame size that killed the app on the Stick
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten

title: tv-app's build script used two deprecated Gradle/Kotlin DSL calls
body:
## Summary
tv-app/build.gradle.kts used android.kotlinOptions and `by tasks.registering(Copy::class)`, both deprecated; every script recompile warned four times.

## Description
kotlinOptions (tv-app/build.gradle.kts:34 before) is deprecated by the Kotlin Gradle plugin in favour of compilerOptions and becomes an error in later plugins, so a Kotlin bump would break the build; tasks.registering (:102 before) is deprecated with 'see the Gradle 9.6 upgrading guide'. deathride's modules already use kotlin { compilerOptions { ... } }. Fixed with that form and tasks.register<Copy>("syncCompanion").

## Flow
- any change to tv-app/build.gradle.kts -> script recompile -> 4 'w:' deprecation lines
- fix: kotlin { compilerOptions { jvmTarget.set(JVM_17) } }; val syncCompanion = tasks.register<Copy>(...)

## Expected impact
Whoever bumps Kotlin or Gradle next does not meet a build error here. Could break: the jvmTarget or the companion copy (both checked).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - no deprecated DSL in the build script
Before: 4 deprecation warnings on a recompile (2 sites)
After: 0 warnings; class files still major 61; syncCompanion still runs before mergeDebugAssets and companion/index.html is in the merged assets
Method: gate - gradlew :tv-app:compileDebugKotlin :tv-app:testDebugUnitTest :tv-app:mergeDebugAssets exit 0, warnings counted in the log on both sides
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
before: w: tv-app/build.gradle.kts:34:5 'kotlinOptions' is deprecated; w: tv-app/build.gradle.kts:102:28 'registering' is deprecated (x3)
after: 0 'w:' lines for tv-app/build.gradle.kts

title: compose ui-tooling-preview shipped in the release APK with no @Preview
body:
## Summary
implementation(libs.compose.ui.tooling.preview) put the preview annotation library on the release classpath, and tv-app has no @Preview.

## Description
tv-app/build.gradle.kts declared it as implementation; `grep -rn "@Preview\|ui.tooling" tv-app/src` returns 0 hits. debugImplementation(compose.ui.tooling) stays for the layout inspector. Fixed by removing the one line.

## Flow
- releaseRuntimeClasspath resolves androidx.compose.ui:ui-tooling-preview and -android for zero consumers
- fix: drop implementation(libs.compose.ui.tooling.preview)

## Expected impact
A smaller release classpath and SBOM (sbom.yml attests the debug APK's runtime classpath). Could break: a future @Preview needs the line back.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - no unused library on the release classpath
Before: 139 resolved modules on releaseRuntimeClasspath (BOM constraint lines excluded)
After: 137; the two removed are ui-tooling-preview and ui-tooling-preview-android
Method: gate - :tv-app:dependencies --configuration releaseRuntimeClasspath counted on both sides; tv-app gate exit 0 (29 tests)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
grep -rn "@Preview\|ui.tooling" tv-app/src -> 0
diff mods-before mods-after: < androidx.compose.ui:ui-tooling-preview, < androidx.compose.ui:ui-tooling-preview-android

title: Any app on the TV could repoint the release build's pairing via launch extras
body:
## Summary
MainActivity is exported and read transport / relay_url / phone_url from any launching intent, so another app could start a release build dialling its relay with the pairing QR (PIN in the fragment) pointing at its page.

## Description
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/MainActivity.kt chooseTransport() honoured the extras unconditionally. They are the harness's switch (tools/relay-test.mjs relaunches the installed debug APK with them). Technique: device-pairing / token-binding-and-transport (the minted credential, here the PIN in the pairing URL, must go only where the owner chose). Fixed: relayRequest(extra, debuggable) honours them only when FLAG_DEBUGGABLE is set. Pair of the stick-app finding 'Any app on the stick can repoint it through the exported url extra'.

## Flow
- another app: startActivity(dev.telestrator.tv/.MainActivity, transport=relay, relay_url=ws://evil/tv, phone_url=http://evil/) -> the TV dials evil -> the QR sends the viewer's phone and PIN to evil
- fix: release builds ignore the extras and listen on the LAN

## Expected impact
A release build's pairing can only point where the build chose. Could break: someone who launched a release build with the relay extras (no harness does) gets LAN.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - launch extras cannot repoint a release build's pairing
Before: LaunchTransportTest: release + relay extras -> RelayRequest(ws://attacker.example/tv, http://attacker.example/)
After: release + extras -> null (LAN); debug + extras -> the relay (unchanged); no extras -> LAN
Method: gate - LaunchTransportTest red on the release case, green after; tv-app gate exit 0 (32 tests). Not run: relay-test.mjs on an emulator
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/MainActivity.kt relayRequest(extra, debuggable): if (!debuggable || extra("transport") != "relay") return null
tv-app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:25 android:exported="true"

title: The phone's thumbnail is the nearest keyframe, not the paused frame
body:
## Summary
Thumbnailer pulls frames with OPTION_CLOSEST_SYNC, so the picture the phone draws over can be up to half a GOP away from the frame the TV shows.

## Description
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/Thumbnailer.kt:14 promises 'the frame the viewer is looking at'; :80 asks MediaMetadataRetriever for the closest SYNC frame. The fixture is encoded with -g 25 at 25 fps (fixtures/README.md:10), one keyframe a second, so a pause between keyframes yields a thumbnail up to 0.5 s off; the fixture's orange box moves ~140 px/s, so up to ~70 px of 1280 (5.5 % of the width) away from where the TV shows it. Real footage has longer GOPs (2-10 s). OPTION_CLOSEST returns the exact frame at the cost of decoding from the previous keyframe. Technique: media-playback / transport-contract (the phone's picture must match the engine's state).

## Flow
- pause the TV at t = 10.48 s -> heartbeat asks dataUrlAt(10480) -> CLOSEST_SYNC returns the 10.0 s keyframe -> the phone shows the box ~67 px left of the TV's box -> the viewer draws on the wrong spot
- fix: OPTION_CLOSEST in RetrieverFrameSource.frameAt, then measure the decode cost on the Stick (the heartbeat waits for the thumbnail before sending state, PenSessionHost.kt:129-132)

## Expected impact
Viewers drawing from the phone hit what they see on the TV. Could break: a slower decode delays the state heartbeat once per pause on the Stick.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the phone's picture is the TV's paused frame
Before: simulation - fixture GOP 25 at 25 fps: worst-case offset 0.5 s = ~70 px at 140 px/s; three pauses (10.04, 10.48, 10.96 s) -> keyframes 10.0, 10.0, 11.0 s -> offsets 6, 67, 6 px
After: predicted 0 s offset under OPTION_CLOSEST; the decode cost on the Stick is the unknown
Method: simulation - the retriever runs only on a device; no JVM decoder
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: Stick run: pause at 10 points between keyframes, record dataUrlAt latency and the orange box's x in the thumbnail vs the TV capture, under CLOSEST_SYNC and CLOSEST

title: Two spotlights at once: the second dims the first's highlight
body:
## Summary
drawSpotlight dims the whole picture and punches its hole once per spotlight, so a second spotlight paints a fresh dim layer over the first one's hole.

## Description
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/Overlay.kt:51 calls drawSpotlight per spotlight; :140-155 each draws a 0.6-alpha black rect over the content rect, then BlendMode.Clear for its own circle. With two visible spotlights, hole 1 is cleared and then covered by rect 2 (0.6 dim, the same as a lone spotlight's outside), the outside is dimmed twice (1 - 0.4 x 0.4 = 0.84), and only the last spotlight reads as highlighted. Core puts no limit on concurrent spotlights. Fix: one dim rect per frame, then every hole, then every ring (also drops the per-frame filterIsInstance list).

## Flow
- draw spotlight A on a player, then B on another, both on the paused frame -> TV shows A's player dimmed and B's player lit
- fix: dim once, clear all holes, draw all rings

## Expected impact
Coaches can highlight two players at once, which is the point of a spotlight in a two-player play. Could break: the Clear blend's interaction with the SurfaceView on the Stick, which only a device shows.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - every spotlight on screen is lit
Before: simulation - two spotlights: hole A alpha 0.6, hole B 0, outside 0.84
After: predicted: holes A and B 0, outside 0.6 (the same as one spotlight)
Method: simulation - compositing arithmetic from the draw order; no JVM canvas and no device capture this session
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: device or emulator capture of two concurrent spotlights (pixel alpha inside each hole and outside) before and after

title: The pairing card never says what to do; its one line of prose is 'via lan'
body:
## Summary
The first thing a viewer sees is a QR, six digits, a URL and 'via lan', with no instruction to scan it with a phone or what the PIN is for.

## Description
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/PairingCard.kt:115-125 (Invitation) draws the QR, Pin, the display URL and stringResource(R.string.link_via, transport) ('via %1$s', tv-app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml:6), which prints the transport's internal name ('lan' / 'relay'). A first-time viewer is not told that the phone is the pen or that the QR opens it; the transport name is diagnostics already on the Menu status line (MainActivity.kt status Text). Fix: one call-to-action line ('Scan with your phone to draw') in strings.xml in place of the via line.

## Flow
- first launch -> card shows QR + 482913 + 192.168.1.20:8765 + 'via lan' -> viewer does not know the phone is the input
- fix: replace link_via with a call to action; keep the transport name on the Menu status line

## Expected impact
First-time viewers pair without being told by someone who knows. Could break: the live UI harness if it reads the via line (it reads testTag pin/status).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the card says what to do
Before: lines of instruction on the Invite card: 0; developer terms shown: 1 ('lan')
After: 1 instruction line, 0 developer terms
Method: simulation - copy count from the composable; the effect on time-to-pair needs viewers and a device
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: device capture of the Invite card before/after, plus a first-run walk timing scan-to-first-stroke for 3 viewers

title: The 30 Hz playhead tick recomposes the whole TV screen, not just the overlay
body:
## Summary
TelestratorScreen keeps the playhead in Compose state it reads in its own body, so every 33 ms tick recomposes the screen composable and everything it calls, including the pairing card.

## Description
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/MainActivity.kt:195 `var tMs by remember { mutableLongStateOf(0L) }` is written every 33 ms (:213) and read in TelestratorScreen's body (passed to TelestrationOverlay and the status Text), as are paused and rate. Session is an unstable parameter, so PairingCard is not skipped either. Technique: media-playback / playback-clock (a frame clock is not reactive state; consumers sample at their own cadence). Fix: hand the overlay a State<Long>/lambda and read it inside the Canvas draw (draw-phase read), and move the status line's reads into its own small composable.

## Flow
- play the clip -> tick writes tMs -> TelestratorScreen recomposes ~30x/s -> PairingCard, AndroidView update, overlay recompose
- fix: draw-phase read of the playhead; the screen recomposes only on doc, link or peek changes

## Expected impact
Less main-thread work per frame on the Stick, where the overlay budget is 4 ms and GC churn is a measured cost. Could break: the overlay must still redraw when tMs changes (a draw-phase read invalidates draw).

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - screen recompositions per second of playback
Before: simulation - ~30 recompositions/s of TelestratorScreen during playback (one per tick) from the read sites
After: predicted ~0/s of the screen body; overlay draws stay ~30/s
Method: simulation - recomposition counts need the Layout Inspector or a counter on a device
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: recomposition counter (SideEffect counter in TelestratorScreen and PairingCard, or Layout Inspector) over 10 s of playback on the Stick, plus RenderStats p95, before and after

title: Voice probe's firstAudioMs loses its index when a line starts and then errors
body:
## Summary
VoiceProbeActivity appends to firstAudioMs on onStart and again (-1) on onError, so a line that starts and then fails writes two entries and every later index is shifted, against the report's own documented shape.

## Description
tv-app/src/debug/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/voiceprobe/VoiceProbeActivity.kt:30 documents 'firstAudioMs[i] is -1 for a line that never started'; :104 onStart appends the latency and :107 onError appends -1. An utterance can call onStart then onError (an engine that fails mid-line), giving 13 entries for 12 lines, and the operator's device run (docs/concepts/NATIVE-VOICE-STACK.md) reads the wrong latency for every later line. Fix: put by index (pass * lines.size + i) and write -1 only if that index never started.

## Flow
- line 3 starts (put 210) then errors (put -1) -> array [.., 210, -1, <line 4>, ..] -> line 4 reads -1
- fix: firstAudioMs.put(index, value); onError writes -1 only when no start was recorded

## Expected impact
The operator's TTS latency figures per line stay true on an engine that errors. Could break: nothing outside the debug probe.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the report matches its documented shape
Before: simulation - three runs: all lines OK -> 12 entries aligned; one never-started line -> 12 aligned; one start-then-error line -> 13 entries, 9 misaligned (if it is line 3)
After: predicted: 12 entries aligned in all three
Method: simulation - org.json is a stub on the JVM, so a test needs the recorder extracted into plain Kotlin first
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
tv-app/src/debug/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/voiceprobe/VoiceProbeActivity.kt:104 override fun onStart(u: String?) { firstAudioMs.put(SystemClock.elapsedRealtime() - asked) }
:107 override fun onError(u: String?) { firstAudioMs.put(-1); ... }
instrument: extract an index-keyed recorder (plain Kotlin) and a src/testDebug test driving start/error sequences

title: The remote cannot step a frame or redo; only the phone can
body:
## Summary
Without a phone, the remote's Left/Right jump by SEEK_HOP_MS and Up undoes, but nothing steps one frame or redoes, though core plans both.

## Description
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/TransportPlan.kt:52-55 plans 'step' (pause + one FRAME_MS) and :72 'redo'; the phone has both (companion/index.html:608, :612-613). The remote map (tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/MainActivity.kt remoteCommand) reaches toggle, play, pause, seek+/-, undo and clear. Finding the exact frame of a play is the Telestrator's core job, and the remote is 'the fallback path when no phone is paired' (MainActivity.kt onKeyDown doc). A mapping (e.g. Left/Right step while paused and seek while playing; Rewind/FF always seek) is a product call on what the keys mean.

## Flow
- paused, no phone -> Right -> seek+ hops SEEK_HOP_MS -> the frame wanted is between hops -> no way to reach it from the remote
- proposal: owner chooses the paused-key meaning; then remoteCommand gains a paused flag and a test

## Expected impact
Remote-only reviewers can land on any frame and recover an undo. Could break: muscle memory for Left/Right while paused.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - frame-accurate review from the remote alone
Before: player verbs reachable from the remote: 7 of 9 (no step, no redo)
After: 9 of 9 under a chosen mapping
Method: simulation - the count is from code; whether reviewers want it is the owner's call
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction

title: The pen listener admits any peer address class before the PIN gate
body:
## Summary
LanTransport binds 0.0.0.0 and serves /, /health and /ws to any peer, with no address-class check in front of the pairing gate, which the governing technique names as layer one.

## Description
Technique: device-pairing / admission-scoping ('classify the peer before you compute'; 'bind-address and peer-class must agree; test the refusal'). tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/transport/LanTransport.kt:111 binds host 0.0.0.0, and penServer (:159-160) answers /health (session telemetry: annotations, pens, playhead) and opens /ws for every peer. The intended audience is the LAN: private, link-local and loopback (adb forward arrives as 127.0.0.1; the emulator host as 10.0.2.2). A TV with a public or carrier-NAT address, or a port-forward, exposes the pairing door and the PIN guess budget to the internet. Fix: an isAdmissiblePeer(remoteHost) classifier (incl. IPv4-mapped IPv6) refusing others with a cheap 403 before any pairing work, with a unit test.

## Flow
- peer from a public address connects to :8765/ws -> admitted -> may spend the shared wrong-PIN budget (locking out the household)
- fix: classify call.request.local.remoteHost; refuse non-private peers on all three routes

## Expected impact
The pairing door is only reachable from the room's network. Could break: a home network on CGNAT ranges (100.64/10) or an unusual emulator route if the classifier is too strict.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - only LAN peers reach the pairing gate
Before: peer classes refused before the PIN gate: 0
After: all non-loopback/private/link-local peers refused
Method: simulation - the classifier test is S, but whether real living-room networks all fall in the admitted classes needs the harness walk on the emulator and the Stick
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
instrument: isAdmissiblePeer unit test (public, private, link-local, loopback, ::ffff:-mapped) plus live-ui-test.mjs and relay-test.mjs on the emulator to prove adb-forwarded and LAN peers still pair

title: A refused PIN or a failed pen server appears on the card without being announced
body:
## Summary
The Refused and Failed card texts appear and vanish without live-region semantics, so a VoiceView user is never told that their PIN was wrong or that the TV cannot accept pens.

## Description
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/PairingCard.kt:70-83 renders LinkView.Refused (shown for REFUSED_MS = 5 s, core LinkState.kt:92) and LinkView.Failed as plain Text with no Modifier.semantics { liveRegion = LiveRegionMode.Polite }. Focus never moves to the card (it is not focusable), so a screen reader only reads it if the user navigates there, and the refusal is gone after 5 s. Distinct from the filed 'paired dot has no semantics'. Fix: a polite live region on the card's title Text for Refused, Failed and Lost.

## Flow
- VoiceView on -> phone offers a wrong PIN -> card shows 'Wrong PIN' for 5 s -> nothing is spoken
- fix: liveRegion = Polite on the title text of Refused / Failed / Lost

## Expected impact
Blind or low-vision viewers hear why pairing failed. Could break: chatty announcements if the poll re-emits the same state (StateFlow dedups equal states).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - state changes on the card are announced
Before: live regions on the card: 0 of 3 transient states
After: 3 of 3
Method: simulation - announcement needs VoiceView on a device; Compose semantics tests need androidTest, which tv-app does not have
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: VoiceView walk on the Stick: wrong PIN from the phone, then the relay down, listening for the announcement before/after

title: No CI job runs tv-app's 32 JVM tests
body:
## Summary
quality.yml runs the desk gate and :core:test; capabilities(-pr).yml build :tv-app:assembleDebug; nothing runs :tv-app:testDebugUnitTest, so the 32 tv-app tests only run when an agent runs them.

## Description
`grep -rn "tv-app" .github/workflows/*.yml` finds only the fixture setup and assembleDebug (capabilities.yml:52, capabilities-pr.yml:58) and SBOM comments; AGENTS.md's gate for tv-app is `:core:test :tv-app:compileDebugKotlin`. This round's frame cap, relay failure, key-repeat and launch-extras guards (and the earlier Session threading, pen count and Thumbnailer tests) can regress unseen. The workflows and AGENTS.md belong to repo-governance, so this is out of this round's paths. Pair of the stick-app finding 'No CI job, gate table or manifest capability runs the stick-app tests'.

## Flow
- a PR breaks Session's pen count -> quality.yml green (no tv-app tests) -> merged
- fix: add :tv-app:testDebugUnitTest to the capabilities build step (it already has the fixture) and to AGENTS.md's tv-app gate row

## Expected impact
tv-app regressions surface on the PR. Could break: CI minutes (the suite ran in ~20 s here).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - tv-app tests run in CI
